legacy_cells.B: Hybrid Digital Twin Framework for Personalized Diabetes Management Using Mathematical Modelling and Machine Learning
legacy_cells.C: Vathana Dennish; Babu Subramani; Vijayakumar Ponnusamy; Suganthi Kuppusamy; Janardhanan Subramonia Kumar; Nemanja Zdravković; Miloš Kostić
legacy_cells.I: 021_2026_Hybrid Digital Twin Framework for Personalized Diabetes Management Using Mathematical Modelling and Machine Learning.pdf
legacy_cells.O: Diabetes mellitus; diabetic and prediabetic volunteers
legacy_cells.S: Can glucose at the next step be forecast from the current glucose–insulin state and lifestyle inputs?
legacy_cells.T: 201 volunteers, age 25–78 years, including diabetic and prediabetic participants
legacy_cells.V: Insulin-dose and lifestyle recommendations to support diabetes management
legacy_cells.AI: Glucose/CGM readings; insulin level and dose/medication; carbohydrate/food intake; physical activity; sleep duration; patient-specific physiological parameters
legacy_cells.BD: Carbohydrate intake: 0–150 g/meal; physical activity: 0–10 MET·h/day; insulin: 0–20 U; sleep duration; medication input
legacy_cells.BI: Hybrid DT for Personalized Glucose Prediction
legacy_cells.BL: 6 min sampling interval; 24 h simulation; glucose prediction horizon reported as one step ahead
legacy_cells.BN: Bergman Minimal Model and Hovorka physiological equations; circadian insulin-sensitivity term; glucose/insulin transition equations
legacy_cells.BP: 10 prior glucose values are provided to the LSTM
legacy_cells.BS: Next-step glucose and insulin states; hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia risk probabilities
legacy_cells.BT: LSTM glucose prediction; Bayesian hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia risk estimation; SHAP feature attribution
legacy_cells.DQ: 201 volunteers (data section); 240 training and 60 testing samples (validation section); relationship between these counts is unclear
legacy_cells.EB: Qualitative simulated responses are described: glucose rises after carbohydrate intake and falls during/after physical activity; no quantitative action-sensitivity analysis is reported.
legacy_cells.ER: SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre Institutional Ethics Committee, approval 8274/IEC/2022; informed consent reported
legacy_cells.FL: Patient glucose/insulin and lifestyle inputs feed a physiology-based glucose–insulin transition (Bergman/Hovorka equations, circadian sensitivity, and LSTM); Bayesian risk estimation and SHAP support a decision-support output. No evaluated planner is described.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors combine physiological glucose–insulin modelling, lifestyle and circadian factors, probabilistic metabolic-risk estimation, and explainability in a personalized diabetes digital-twin framework.
legacy_cells.FN: The paper reports one-step prediction and five-fold metrics (RMSE 14.982 ± 0.688; MAE 12.467 ± 0.572; R² 0.094 ± 0.297). It also reports a 24 h simulation at 6 min sampling intervals and a Digital Twin prediction time of 0.003364 s.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors state that patient-specific calibration and parameter tuning are required; they also identify dependence on high-quality sensor data and uninterrupted connectivity, and note that physiological variability, sensor noise, and missing data may reduce accuracy.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors propose connecting real-time CGM, validating on clinical datasets, improving personalization and interpretability, adding cloud/interoperability and federated-learning/edge approaches, and conducting multicenter clinical validation.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify limited personalization, lifestyle and circadian modelling, probabilistic risk assessment, explainability, and adaptive decision support in prior diabetes digital-twin approaches.
legacy_cells.FR: Results report a one-step-ahead glucose prediction and internal split/cross-validation, not prospective clinical deployment, improved patient outcomes, identified causal treatment effects, or demonstrated optimization of insulin-dose decisions. The relationship between the stated 201 volunteers and 240/60 training/testing samples is unclear, and reported metric tables are not fully consistent.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Pass the paper’s specified action and time context explicitly into the state-transition interface; preserve the boundary between predictive action sensitivity and identified intervention effects.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF text, pp. 1–26: title/abstract; introduction and related work; architecture and methods; physiological equations, algorithm and data collection; all results and relevant tables; limitations/future work, ethics/data statement, conclusion, and references. Particularly inspected pp. 1, 6–18, and 19–25. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Corrected the prefilled author field to match the PDF byline; preserved the other prefilled A:I fields. Evidence is inconsistent in places: Table 3 is poorly laid out, the reported 201 volunteers do not clearly reconcile with 240/60 training/testing samples, and metric values differ across Tables 4, 5, and 9. The paper explicitly reports one-step-ahead validation; dosing optimization and clinical benefit remain author claims rather than demonstrated clinical outcomes. The supplied materials do not include the KB key for mapping blueprint modules, so FS names the functions without assigning M-numbers. Evidence QA: 65/82 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (79.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 73 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 10 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: No independent human scientific review, code reproduction or supplement inspection.
Primary numerical and mathematical inconsistencies limit confidence; retain exact reported values, no corrective invented numbers.
201volunteers vs300train/test samples and clinical-vs-simulation validation provenance unresolved;R2 not verified.
Volunteer sensor study is distinct from prospective therapeutic DT use; no causal effects or patient benefit established.
